2026-01-00 - STONE HILL STUDIO, COLTS NECK, NJ

A RAINY NIGHT IN SOHO

Some time around late 2025 or very early 2026, Springsteen recorded his cover version of "A Rainy Night In Soho" at Stone Hill Studio. It's not certain if the horn parts were also recorded at this session or overdubbed later. The song was released as a single on March 12, 2026 and included on the various artists tribute album 20th Century Paddy (The Songs Of Shane MacGowan), released on November 16, 2026.


2026-01-17 - HACKENSACK MERIDIAN HEALTH THEATRE, RED BANK, NJ

with Willie Nile: ONE GUITAR (with James Maddock)

with Joe Grushecky & The Houserockers: JOLÉ BLON (with Gary U.S. Bonds, Laurie Anderson, Mark Leimbach, and Joe Grillo) / THIS LITTLE GIRL (with Gary U.S. Bonds, Laurie Anderson, Mark Leimbach, and Joe Grillo) / DARKNESS ON THE EDGE OF TOWN / SAVIN' UP / I'M NOT SLEEPING / PUMPING IRON (with Danny Clinch) / LUCKY TOWN / ATLANTIC CITY / NEVER BE ENOUGH TIME / JOHNNY 99 (with Danny Clinch) / THE PROMISED LAND (with John Rzeznik) / LIGHT OF DAY - HAPPY BIRTHDAY (with all performers) / THUNDER ROAD (with all performers)

Bruce makes a surprise appearance at the twenty-sixth annual Light Of Day Benefit. After a one-song appearance with Willie Nile, he plays a full set backed by Joe Grushecky & The Houserockers, beginning with two songs also featuring Gary U.S. Bonds. Bruce dedicates "The Promised Land" to Renee Good, speaking briefly before the song about ongoing events: "ICE should get the fuck out of Minneapolis." The show closes with an all-hands-on-deck "Light Of Day" (including the "Land Of 1000 Dances" interlude), followed by Bruce leading everyone in singing "Happy Birthday" to Bob Benjamin and the traditional closing "Thunder Road" singalong.


2026-01-27 - STONE HILL STUDIO, COLTS NECK, NJ

STREETS OF MINNEAPOLIS

Inspired by the protests in Minneapolis, MN against ICE, Springsteen wrote "Streets Of Minneapolis" on January 24 and recorded it at this session. The song was released as a digital single the very next day.


2026-01-30 - FIRST AVENUE, MINNEAPOLIS, MN

Soundcheck: STREETS OF MINNEAPOLIS / THE GHOST OF TOM JOAD (with Tom Morello)

STREETS OF MINNEAPOLIS / THE GHOST OF TOM JOAD (with Tom Morello) / POWER TO THE PEOPLE (with all performers)

Bruce takes part in 'A Concert of Solidarity & Resistance to Defend Minnesota!', organized by Tom Morello. He performs an acoustic rendition of "Streets Of Minneapolis" in its live premiere, followed by a version with Morello and his band of "The Ghost Of Tom Joad". The set closes with "Power To The People" featuring all the day's performers, Bruce's first ever performance of the song.


2026-02-01 - CRYPTO.COM ARENA, LOS ANGELES, CA

Bruce Springsteen wasn't at the 68th Annual Grammy Awards ceremony in person, but he was there in voice, via a pre-recorded tribute to the late Brian Wilson of the Beach Boys during the 'In Memoriam' segment. A collage of images was shown, including a picture (see our Gallery tab) of Bruce and Brian together taken backstage of the Count Basie Center in Red Bank, NJ. The Tracks II: The Lost Albums box set won the Grammy Award for Best Recording Package; art directors Meghan Foley and Michelle Holme accepted the award.

2026-03-23 - RIVERSIDE CHURCH, NEW YORK CITY, NY

STREETS OF MINNEAPOLIS / PEOPLE HAVE THE POWER (with all performers)

Bruce makes a surprise appearance at the Democracy Now! 30th Anniversary special event, performing a solo acoustic "Streets Of Minneapolis" and answering a few questions from Amy Goodman before participating in the all-star finale rendition of Patti Smith's "People Have The Power". Other performers include Smith, Michael Stipe, Aaron Dessner, and Hurray For The Riff Raff.

2026-03-28 - MINNESOTA STATE CAPITOL, SAINT PAUL, MN

STREETS OF MINNEAPOLIS

Springsteen, introduced by Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, performs a solo acoustic "Streets Of Minneapolis" at the No Kings Rally at the Minnesota State Capitol. Speakers at the event include U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, Jane Fonda, Lt. Gov. 2026-03-31 - TARGET CENTER, MINNEAPOLIS, MN

WAR (with Tom Morello) / BORN IN THE U.S.A. (with Tom Morello) / DEATH TO MY HOMETOWN (with Tom Morello) / NO SURRENDER / DARKNESS ON THE EDGE OF TOWN / STREETS OF MINNEAPOLIS / THE PROMISED LAND / OUT IN THE STREET / HUNGRY HEART / YOUNGSTOWN / MURDER INCORPORATED / AMERICAN SKIN (41 SHOTS) (with Tom Morello) / LONG WALK HOME (with Tom Morello) / HOUSE OF A THOUSAND GUITARS / MY CITY OF RUINS / BECAUSE THE NIGHT / WRECKING BALL / THE RISING / THE GHOST OF TOM JOAD (with Tom Morello) / BADLANDS (with Tom Morello) / LAND OF HOPE AND DREAMS - PEOPLE GET READY (with Tom Morello) / BORN TO RUN / BOBBY JEAN / DANCING IN THE DARK / TENTH AVENUE FREEZE-OUT (with Tom Morello) / PURPLE RAIN (with Tom Morello) / CHIMES OF FREEDOM (with Tom Morello)

27-song set to open the 2026 Land Of Hope And Dreams - No Kings Tour opens with the first performance of "War" since 2003 into "Born In The U.S.A." (complete with a brief guitar duel with Tom Morello in the outro). "Streets Of Minneapolis" has its first performance with the E Street Band, and local special "Purple Rain" appears in the encores, a tour one-off with fiery guitar work from Morello and Nils Lofgren. Most of the rest of the set takes the same basic shape as the 2025 shows, including the acoustic "House Of A Thousand Guitars" and the speech before "My City Of Ruins". "Long Walk Home" includes the "Land Of Hope And Dreams" guitar intro. Tom Morello appears on several songs throughout the show, as he will throughout the tour. "War", "Streets Of Minneapolis", "American Skin (41 Shots)", "The Ghost Of Tom Joad", and "Purple Rain" all make their first appearances on the combined Land Of Hope And Dreams Tour, including 2025.

2026-04-18 - POLLAK THEATRE, MONMOUTH UNIVERSITY, WEST LONG BRANCH, NJ

LIGHT MY FIRE (with John Densmore) / ROADHOUSE BLUES (with Steve Earle and Mickey Raphael) / THE WEIGHT (with Steve Earle, Darlene Love, and Amy Helm) / THUNDER ROAD (with The E Street Band) / BECAUSE THE NIGHT (with Patti Smith, Tony Shanahan, and John Densmore) / PEOPLE HAVE THE POWER (with all performers)

Bruce Springsteen performs and presents at the fourth annual American Music Honors, a presentation of the Bruce Springsteen Archives & Center For American Music at Monmouth University. The 2026 honorees are Dionne Warwick (inducted by Springsteen), The Doors (inducted by Steven Van Zandt), The Band (posthumously inducted by Max Weinberg, with Amy Helm accepting the award), Dr. Dre (inducted by Jimmy Iovine), The E Street Band (inducted by Jon Landau), and Patti Smith (inducted by Springsteen). Bruce accepts the award for the E Street Band induction on behalf of Patti Scialfa, while Jake Clemons accepts on behalf of Clarence Clemons and Jason Federici accepts on behalf of Danny Federici. The Disciples Of Soul serve as the evening's house band, and Brian Williams emcees; Steve Earle, Public Enemy, Darlene Love, and Mickey Raphael also make surprise appearances.

Standard 27-song set for the tour's closing show. "Two Hearts" includes "It Takes Two"; "Long Walk Home" includes the "Land Of Hope And Dreams" guitar intro. All the evening's songs, with the exceptions of "Clampdown", "Two Hearts", and "American Land", were played at every show of the tour. "Born In The U.S.A.", "Death To My Hometown", "The Promised Land", "Youngstown", "Murder Incorporated", "Long Walk Home", "House Of A Thousand Guitars" (at least in part), "Because The Night", "Wrecking Ball", "The Rising", "Badlands", "Land Of Hope And Dreams", "Born To Run", "Dancing In The Dark", "Tenth Avenue Freeze-Out", and "Chimes Of Freedom" were performed at every show of the combined 2025/2026 Land Of Hope And Dreams Tour. Show rescheduled from May 8.

End of the "Land Of Hope And Dreams - No Kings" tour


2026-06-03 - BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN CENTER FOR AMERICAN MUSIC, MONMOUTH UNIVERSITY, WEST LONG BRANCH, NJ

Bruce takes part in a PBS interview at the new Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music in advance of the Center opening to the public on June 13. It will be broadcast as part of a half-hour TV special titled; "Bruce Springsteen: Finding America in Song".

If you have any information (eg. setlist, memories, ticket stub or other images, as applicable) regarding this date please get in touch.


2026-06-04 - OCEANFIRST BANK CENTER, MONMOUTH UNIVERSITY, WEST LONG BRANCH, NJ

PLANE WRECK AT LOS GATOS (DEPORTEE) (with Rosanne Cash) / THIS LAND IS YOUR LAND (with Kenny Chesney) / I'M SHIPPING UP TO BOSTON (with Dropkick Murphys) / AMERICAN LAND (with Dropkick Murphys) / WHEN THE SAINTS GO MARCHING IN (with Trombone Shorty & The New Breed Brass Band and all performers)

Night one of 'Music America: The Songs that Shaped Us', a two-night, multi-act celebration of America's 250th anniversary presented by the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music. Springsteen concludes the night by performing duets with Rosanne Cash, Kenny Chesney, and Dropkick Murphys; all the evening's artists join Trombone Shorty & New Breed Brass Band for the closing "When The Saints Go Marching In". Other performers are Shemekia Copeland, Valerie June, Keb' Mo', Tony Trischka and Sister Sadie, and Brian Fallon. The Disciples Of Soul serve as the house band, Robert Santelli emcees (providing a running history of American music), and Indigenous Enterprise and a Native American drum circle open the show.


2026-06-05 - OCEANFIRST BANK CENTER, MONMOUTH UNIVERSITY, WEST LONG BRANCH, NJ

JAILHOUSE ROCK / BURNING LOVE / I SHALL BE RELEASED (with Sheryl Crow, Larry Campbell, and Teresa Williams) / FARTHER UP THE ROAD (with Gary Clark Jr., Jimmie Vaughan, and Nils Lofgren) / RAISE YOUR HAND (with Steven Van Zandt, Jon Bon Jovi, Nils Lofgren, Jimmie Vaughan, Public Enemy, Darlene Love, Jackson Browne, and Grace Bowers) / I DON'T WANT TO GO HOME (with Steven Van Zandt, Jon Bon Jovi, Nils Lofgren, Jimmie Vaughan, Public Enemy, Darlene Love, Jackson Browne, and Grace Bowers) / LAND OF HOPE AND DREAMS

Night two of 'Music America: The Songs that Shaped Us', a two-night, multi-act celebration of America's 250th anniversary presented by the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music. Springsteen opens the show with renditions of "Jailhouse Rock" and "Burning Love" and later duets with Sheryl Crow for "I Shall Be Released" before closing the show with three all-star performances and a solo acoustic "Land Of Hope And Dreams". Bruce sings a brief snippet of "My Girl" before "Raise Your Hand". Other performers are Jon Bon Jovi, Steven Van Zandt, Gary Clark Jr., Dion, Darlene Love, David Sancious and Will Calhoun, Jimmie Vaughan, Mavis Staples, Jackson Browne, Nils Lofgren, and Public Enemy. The Disciples Of Soul serve as the house band; Robert Santelli emcees.


2026-06-06 - BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN CENTER FOR AMERICAN MUSIC, MONMOUTH UNIVERSITY, WEST LONG BRANCH, NJ

Bruce Springsteen, speaks at the Bruce Springsteen Center For American Music Dedication ceremony shortly before the center opens to the public, with Patti Scialfa, members of Bruce's family, Jon Landau, and several past and present E Street Band members in attendance, as well as Governor Mikie Sherrill. The event was held in a tent in the Center's parking lot, with about 300 people in attendance. Musical entertainment was provided by the New Breed Brass Band and David Sancious.

Bruce Springsteen is presented the Harry Belafonte Voices for Social Justice Award at the Tribeca Festival. The event features Bono interviewing Springsteen as well as tributes from Robert De Niro and Patti Smith. Bono and Springsteen join Smith on a "People Have The Power" finale, before Bruce returns for a solo acoustic "Land Of Hope And Dreams".

Bruce Springsteen performs at the Grand Opening Ceremony and dedication of the Barack Obama Presidential Center, playing a solo acoustic "Land Of Hope And Dreams" and then joining many of the event's performers for the closing rendition of "Higher Ground" (Bruce's first performance on the song). Additional musical performers include Christina Aguilera, Common, Eddie Vedder, Jennifer Hudson, John Legend, Marc Anthony, The Roots, Stevie Wonder, Tems, and Bono & The Edge.

2026-07-31 - STONE HILL STUDIO, COLTS NECK, NJ

BORN TO RUN

In 1984, Billy Starr, founder and chairman of the Pan-Mass Challenge, wrote a letter to Bruce Springsteen inviting him to appear at the annual bike ride and fundraiser for cancer research at the Dana-Farber Institute in Boston. Forty-two years later, Springsteen surprised riders with a pre-recorded message and acoustic performance of "Born To Run" during the 'State of PMC' event at the College of the Holy Cross in Worcester, MA. Springsteen praised Dana-Farber's research and medical treatment—Patti Scialfa is a patient there—stating that "Now, more than ever, the world needs more everyday heroes like the folks who make up the PMC."

STREETS OF MINNEAPOLIS / CHIMES OF FREEDOM (with Joan Baez) / CLAMPDOWN / THE GHOST OF TOM JOAD / FORTUNATE SON (with Dave Matthews and Nathaniel Rateliff) / ROCKIN' IN THE FREE WORLD (with Dave Grohl and Dave Matthews) THIS LAND IS YOUR LAND (with all performers) / POWER TO THE PEOPLE (with all performers)

Bruce Springsteen joins Tom Morello and his band for the closing set of the Power to the People Festival, a celebration of peace, justice, solidarity, music, and community action curated by Morello. Bruce begins with a solo acoustic "Streets Of Minneapolis" and an acoustic duet with Joan Baez on "Chimes Of Freedom" before being joined by Morello and his band along with various guests. Other performers (with various collaborations between acts) include The Neighborhood Kids, The Last Internationale, State Radio, grandson, The Linda Lindas, "Jack Sabbath" (Jack Black with Roman Morello, Revel Ian, Yoyoka Soma, and Hugo Weiss) featuring Geezer Butler, Killer Mike, Cypress Hill, Nathaniel Rateliff, Morello (featuring Serj Tankian, B-Real, Daryl "D.M.C." McDaniels, and Scott Ian), "Sons of Soundgarden" (Matt Cameron, Mike McCready, Taylor Momsen, Morello, and Robbie Mangano), Public Enemy, Dave Matthews, Baez, Stephen Stills, Dropkick Murphys (featuring Matt Hensley and Michael Fanone), and Foo Fighters, alongside artwork and a DJ set by legendary artist Shepard Fairey.
